methodology_note: Supplemental health/life insurer (Aflac Japan + Aflac U.S.) — not an owner-FCF DCF. Operating/free cash flow for an insurer reflects premium float and investment-portfolio timing, not distributable owner earnings, and GAAP net income/EPS is dominated by non-economic investment mark-to-market noise (FY2025 net earnings fell to $3.6B from $5.4B in FY2024 on net investment losses and CECL allowances even as management's own adjusted EPS hit a record $7.49). Reported shareholders' equity (and therefore BVPS) is itself volatile because it carries AOCI — unrealized gains/losses on the large yen-denominated JGB and USD fixed-income portfolios swing with interest rates (BVPS fell from $46.86 FY2020 to $25.17 FY2021 as rates rose, pure AOCI mechanics, not a change in franchise value). This model follows the same book-value-compounding approach used elsewhere in this project for insurers/holdcos (FRFHF, and the residual-income variant for banks NAB.AX/IAG.AX/SRBK): (1) project BVPS per share forward at a scenario compounding rate that blends underlying (ex-AOCI) earnings retention with the structural per-share tailwind from Aflac's ~5-6%/yr buyback-driven share count decline, fading from the AOCI-recovery-boosted recent run rate toward a more sustainable long-run pace, (2) add back the dividend per share each year (management targets total per-share value creation, not book value net of the payout), (3) apply an exit price-to-book multiple anchored to the post-2022 (AOCI-stabilized) trading range of ~2.0-2.4x, and (4) discount dividends plus the Year-5 terminal value at a cost of equity (never WACC — there is no debt to add back and net debt is held at zero; this is a per-share equity-holder valuation, not an enterprise value).

inputs.notes: Model: BVPS-compounding at cost of equity (insurer route per dcf-methods SKILL.md; deposits/insurance-float analog to NAB.AX/IAG.AX residual-income and FRFHF's BVPS-compounding — never owner-FCF). No prior AFL DCF/Drivers file existed; this is a fresh build. net_debt held at 0 throughout — Aflac's balance sheet is a life/health insurer's invested portfolio funding policy reserves, not operating net debt, and capitalizing an already-post-financing per-share flow (BVPS growth + dividend) at cost of equity would double-count leverage if net debt were subtracted again. total_debt line on the balance sheet (senior notes, ~$7-8B) funds the investment portfolio backing policy liabilities, not a claim to be netted off equity value. A 2-for-1 stock split occurred in Q4 2016 (827.841 shares FY2016 vs 411.14m Q3 2016) — all CAGRs below use FY2017 onward only, fully post-split.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend: bvps_8yr_cagr_post_split (structural) + buyback pace, faded from 3yr run-rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: BVPS CAGRs are dominated by AOCI (interest-rate mark-to-market on the JGB/USD fixed-income book), not by earnings power: the 3yr figure (20.4%) is inflated by recovery from a 2021-2022 rate-shock trough in AOCI, while the 5yr figure (3.3%) is depressed by starting from an artificially high FY2020 base (near-zero-rate AOCI peak). Revenue CAGRs (-3.6%/-5.0%) are negative almost entirely on USD/JPY translation (yen weakened from ~110 to ~155-160 over the period) with underlying Japan yen-denominated premium broadly stable to growing — not a shrinking business. EPS CAGRs are near-zero because FY2025 GAAP EPS ($6.82) was depressed ~29% YoY by net investment losses/CECL allowances against a record FY2025 management-adjusted EPS of $7.49; GAAP EPS is not used as the growth anchor for this reason. The 8-year post-split BVPS CAGR (7.5%, FY2017-FY2025) spans a full rate cycle (near-zero through 2021, JGB shock 2022, recovery to >3% 10yr JGB yields by 2026) and is the most defensible structural anchor; it is blended with the current ~5.3-5.9%/yr buyback-driven share-count decline (which mechanically adds to per-share BVPS growth beyond retained-earnings growth alone) to select a fading base-case path starting near 11% and settling at 8%.
historical_growth.note_dividend_drag: Unlike FRFHF (where the projected BVPS growth rate is set GROSS of the dividend, i.e. total value creation, and the $15/share payout is then subtracted each year in the compounding formula before the dividend is separately discounted), the AFL bvps_growth_rates below are applied directly to the raw historical CAGRs, which are themselves NET of dividend already (reported shareholders equity/BVPS falls by the dividend paid, same as any company). The dividend per share is discounted as a separate cash flow to shareholders WITHOUT subtracting it again from the compounding BVPS path — subtracting it twice would double-count roughly a 4%/yr drag (current dividend yield on BVPS is $2.44/$59.96 = 4.1%) and understate intrinsic value. This is a deliberate deviation from the FRFHF file`s formula, made because AFL`s ~35-40% payout ratio (vs FRFHF`s near-100%-of-book-growth flat $15 dividend) makes the gross-up convention a much larger, harder-to-calibrate assumption here; net-of-dividend is the more conservative, better-grounded choice given the historical data available.
historical_growth.note_split: FY2015 BVPS ($40.88) is pre-2-for-1-split and not comparable to post-split figures; excluded from all CAGR calculations above.

base.description: BVPS growth fades from an above-trend 11% (reflecting continued JGB reinvestment-yield tailwind as 10yr JGB yields sit above 3%, a 30-year high, plus the ~5-6%/yr buyback pace) toward a more sustainable 8% by Year 5 as the rate tailwind normalizes and Japan's demographic ceiling reasserts itself. Dividend grows from the current $2.44/yr run-rate at ~7-8%/yr, consistent with the pattern of Aflac's 40+ consecutive years of annual increases (most recently +5.2% effective Q1 2026) plus continued capital-return capacity. Exit P/B of 2.0x sits at the low end of the post-2022 AOCI-stabilized trading range (2.05x-2.37x FY2022-FY2025 year-end), conservative relative to the current 1.90x on Q2-2026 BVPS given the improving reinvestment-yield backdrop.

bull.description: JGB yields continue rising and the reinvestment tailwind persists longer, Japan sales momentum from the 2025 product launches (Miraito, Onsen Tallett, repriced Tsumitasu) sustains above-guidance growth, U.S. net earned premium re-accelerates into the top of the 3-6% CAGR range, and buybacks continue at the current ~$4B/yr pace without capital-ratio strain. Exit P/B of 2.3x, near but below the FY2024 year-end peak (2.37x).

bear.description: Yen weakness resumes or JGB yields plateau, eroding the reinvestment tailwind; Japan demographic decline and intensifying U.S. voluntary-benefits competition (Guardian and others in dental/vision) cap organic growth; the unresolved cybersecurity class action (motion to dismiss denied August 2026) produces a material litigation/remediation charge; capital ratios tighten and the buyback pace slows. Exit P/B of 1.5x, below the entire post-2022 range, reflecting a de-rating scenario.

scenario_narratives.base: Rising JGB yields keep turning a decade-long reinvestment headwind into a tailwind; Japan sales recover on 2025's new-product slate; U.S. premium grows within the low end of the 3-6% guided range; buybacks continue retiring ~5-6% of shares annually. BVPS compounds from $59.96 to ~$93.50 by Year 5; exit at 2.0x book.
scenario_narratives.bull: JGB tailwind persists and steepens further, Japan sales momentum exceeds the 'above 2025 levels' guidance, U.S. premium growth re-accelerates toward the top of its range, and the capital-return program is undisturbed. BVPS reaches ~$105.60 by Year 5; exit at 2.3x book, near the post-2022 high.
scenario_narratives.bear: Yen weakness resumes, JGB yields plateau, Japan's demographic ceiling bites, U.S. competition intensifies, and cybersecurity litigation produces a material charge that also slows buybacks. BVPS grows to only ~$74.00 by Year 5; multiple de-rates to 1.5x book, below the entire post-2022 trading range.

sensitivity.row_axis: bvps_growth_rate_pct (avg of 5yr path, base path shifted uniformly)
sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows are the average annual BVPS growth rate (base 5-yr path of [11,10,9,8.5,8]% shifted -4/-2/0/+2/+4pp uniformly, average shown), columns are exit price-to-book multiple (1.6x-2.4x) applied to Year-5 BVPS. Cost of equity held at base case 9.0%. Field names (wacc_range/terminal_growth_range) retained for dashboard compatibility even though the axes here are BVPS growth and exit P/B, not WACC and perpetuity growth, per insurer-specific book-value-compounding methodology (see FRFHF for the same convention).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. Bear held at 25% rather than lower because AFL carries two live, high-severity, hard-to-quantify tail risks simultaneously (unresolved cybersecurity class action with a denied motion to dismiss as of August 2026, and structural Japan yen/demographic exposure to >50% of earnings) — not a symmetric operating-risk profile.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)

valuation_philosophy.summary: Aflac is a supplemental health/life insurer where GAAP net income, GAAP EPS, and operating/free cash flow are all poor proxies for owner earnings in any single year: net income swings on non-economic net investment losses and CECL allowances (FY2025 GAAP EPS $6.82 vs management's own record adjusted EPS of $7.49), and reported shareholders' equity carries AOCI mark-to-market on a large yen-denominated JGB and USD fixed-income book that swings with interest rates independent of underlying franchise value (BVPS fell 46% in FY2021 on rate mechanics alone). This model therefore compounds BVPS per share forward at a scenario growth rate (capturing both underlying earnings retention and the structural per-share lift from Aflac's persistent ~5-6%/yr buyback-driven share-count decline), adds back the dividend, applies an exit price-to-book multiple anchored to the post-2022 AOCI-stabilized trading range (2.05x-2.37x), and discounts dividends plus the Year-5 terminal value at a cost of equity — never WACC, since net debt is held at zero throughout (the balance sheet funds policy reserves, not operating leverage to net off).
key_risks_to_valuation: Yen/dollar translation: >50% of earnings originate in Japan; sustained yen weakness mechanically depresses USD-reported BVPS growth and dividends even if yen-denominated economics are unchanged
AOCI/interest-rate sensitivity: a renewed decline in JGB or U.S. rates would compress reported BVPS via unrealized bond losses, independent of the underlying insurance business

Unresolved cybersecurity litigation (June 2025 breach, ~22.65 million individuals; motion to dismiss denied August 2026) carries open-ended remediation, litigation, and reputational cost not sized in any scenario

Exit multiple risk: the entire post-2022 P/B anchor range (2.05x-2.37x) reflects a period of rising/high rates improving reinvestment yields; a return to a near-zero-rate regime could compress the sustainable multiple below the bear case's 1.5x floor

Japan demographic decline structurally caps the core cancer/medical addressable market, requiring continual costly product renewal (Miraito, Onsen Tallett, Tsumitasu) just to sustain flat-to-growing sales
